about: What a festival's crier calls at the square (Docs/Design/56-fame-and-memory.md, 7): an opening, up to `deedsMost` deeds from the town's word since the last festival (heaviest first; only deeds that travel under a name: the user, 2026-10-08), the nicknames coined in town that season, and a closing, a line a minute. Blanks: {town}, {festival}, {name} (the name the deed travels under), {deed} (what was done, after 'who'), {nickname}. One line of each list is chosen by hash. A legendary deed is called in every town at noon the day after.
opening: Hear ye, folk of {town}! At {festival}, the town remembers its own!
Gather round, gather round! {festival}, and the deeds of the season!
Hear ye! Before the night is out, {town} would have you know who did it proud!
great: Hear ye, all! {name} {deed}! {town} will not forget it!
Mark it well: {name} {deed}, and {town} owes them!
legendary: Hear ye, hear ye! Word from far and wide: {name} {deed}!
closing: That's the season's tale. Eat, drink, and be glad of each other!
So ends the calling. Good night to you, {town}!
Remember them! And now, the night is yours.
